title: Extend Rust HTML page builder with CSS, headings, tables, and navigation
description: A minimal Rust HTML page builder has basic paragraph support. Extend it with CSS injection, multi-level headings, full HTML tables, and a navigation bar, plus comprehensive tests for all new features.

task_spec.prompt: The rust-page-builder crate has a Page struct with new(), add_paragraph(), and render(). Extend it: 1. Add CSS injection: pub fn with_css(&mut self, css: &str) -> &mut Self - Injects inside the block (after ). - Multiple calls append multiple <style> blocks. 2. Add headings: pub fn add_heading(&mut self, level: u8, text: &str) -> &mut Self - Appends <h{level}>{text}</h{level}> to the body. - level must be 1–6 (inclusive). Panic with 'heading level must be 1–6' if out of range. 3. Add HTML table: pub fn add_table(&mut self, headers: &[&str], rows: &[&[&str]]) -> &mut Self - Appends a <table> with a <thead> row of <th> cells and <tbody> rows of <td> cells. - Empty headers slice → just an empty <table></table>. 4. Add navigation bar: pub fn add_nav(&mut self, links: &[(&str, &str)]) -> &mut Self - Each tuple is (href, label). - Renders <nav><ul><li><a href="{href}">{label}</a></li>...</ul></nav>. - Empty links slice → <nav><ul></ul></nav>. 5. Add 8 new tests: - test_with_css: render contains <style>body{color:red;}</style> - test_multiple_css: render contains two <style> blocks - test_add_heading_h1: render contains <h1>Title</h1> - test_add_heading_h3: render contains <h3>Sub</h3> - test_add_heading_invalid: std::panic::catch_unwind confirms panic on level=0 - test_add_table_basic: render contains <th>Name</th> and <td>Alice</td> - test_add_nav_basic: render contains <a href="/home">Home</a> - test_add_nav_empty: render contains <nav><ul></ul></nav> All 3 existing tests must still pass. Run cargo test to confirm.
required_artifacts: with_css(&mut self, css: &str) -> &mut Self adds <style> in head
add_heading(&mut self, level: u8, text: &str) -> &mut Self with panic on invalid level
followup_prompts: Good. Now handle edge cases: what does the UI show when data is empty, loading, or an error occurs? Add those states and tests.
Run `cargo test` to verify the complete implementation. Fix any failures and confirm all UI states work correctly.
